card.name: Lab value changes prompting dose adjustment
card.fires_on: Words ending or continuing a lab-value phrase (hemoglobin, glucose, platelet counts, PTH, tumor cell lysis) in dosing instructions. It fires where the text is about to say to reduce, interrupt or adjust treatment.

modes.label: Lab unit or term end
modes.description: The last piece of a lab measure or lab term, such as g/dL or lysis, in a dose-adjustment rule.
modes.example: If hemoglobin exceeds 12 g/d<<L>> , interrupt treatment with JESDUV

modes.label: Direction of lab change
modes.description: A verb or adjective saying a lab value rises, falls or is abnormally low, before a dose change.
modes.example: Suspend or decrease the dose if intact PTH is persistently and abnormally<< low>> to reduce the risk of adynamic bone

card.writes: It seems to add words like 'unwanted' or 'too much', pointing toward over-response or an excess to be avoided.
card.plain: It marks the point in a dosing rule where a lab value is named or its change is described, just before the instruction to adjust the dose.
